## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13) is a verse narrative preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text illustrates the karmic consequences of greed and failing to practice generosity [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
While SuttaCentral identifies no curated external parallels for the text [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus registers substantial formulaic overlap across 20 other Pali canonical and paracanonical works [DharmaNexus]. Besides extensive alignment with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the story shares recurring verse segments (§7.6–12.4) with several closely related narratives in the *Petavatthu*, specifically the *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15), the *Sāriputtattheramātupetivatthu* (Pv 14), and the *Nandāpetivatthu* (Pv 16) [DharmaNexus]. Additional textual reuse within the *Petavatthu* occurs with the *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31, §0.3–4.1), the *Sāṇavāsītherapetavatthu* (Pv 27), and the *Dhanapālaseṭṭhipetavatthu* (Pv 19) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, a stock passage (§10.1–12.4) is shared with multiple discourses of the *Vimānavatthu*, including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dīpavimānavatthu* (Vv 9), *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), *Paṭhamasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 13), *Dutiyasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 14), *Uttarāvimānavatthu* (Vv 15), and *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), as well as the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated matches, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring segment reuses with Tibetan texts, such as the *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144) and the *Āyuṣparyanta-sūtra* (D0307) [DharmaNexus].
